run_by: Claude (weight-research-fable). The conversion and the path order were worked out with Astra (weight-research-astra), who also built the complete correspondence this run takes its target from.
hypothesis: The capability leaves a recurring difference between the traces of correct and wrong answers, from where the two shared patterns part until they reconcile. Changing the weights so that, over that stretch, the wrong answers' own computation is brought to where the correct pattern is right after each matrix has written, and stays where it was everywhere else, repairs the capability: the edited model, answering on its own, does the calculation the correct answers do.
what_went_wrong_before: Four edits were built for the A rung and none of them tested the hypothesis, because the model failed before the calculation. a2 fitted 750 inputs to the plain difference of the group means (52% of the attention matrices changed). a2-pattern divided the gap of the merged signal by the learned scale, which asked for 64% and 33% of the outputs where the move is 15 to 17% of the turn. a2-sent and a2-diverge asked in what each matrix sends (3% of each matrix) but were fitted on the wrong group's average input per place with nothing held: where a matrix was asked for nothing the built edit still changed its output by a quarter to two thirds of what it did where it was asked, and the model, answering on its own, left the path at the ninth token, where the two groups follow each other. All four sized all 70 matrices on the original inputs and applied them together, so the corrections of earlier matrices were not seen by later ones (in a2-sent's dropped replay they added up to 1.5 times the gap in layers 15 to 19). The alignment they used kept 22,349 of the 30,546 generated steps. A fifth miss was caught before anything was built. This run first declared the ask as the shared gap in the turn of each merge. Added up along the path, with the turns of the third merges held as they are in the original, those asks would leave the state further from the correct pattern than no edit from the middle layers on, and at the first merge 98% of the ask was the gap of the token embeddings, which no weight produces (state-overlap keeps the record). The first solver also chose its ridge on a closed-form approximation and then applied a different, exact solve; chosen on the edit actually applied, the ridge is weaker and the edit larger.
why_this_direction: Marcos, November 9: the ratio is different per layer and has to be reversed correctly from the trace to the weights, it may be more than a ratio and may need to be overlap aware; the change has to take into account the influence every layer has on the next; it belongs only where the patterns diverge, from where they part until they reconcile; and the test is the edited model's own answers and their traces. Each of those is now a measured fact, not only a direction: (1) input-overlap: where the patterns diverge, what arrives at each matrix differs between the groups by 3.7 times chance (halves agree 0.79), at every depth, and where the groups follow each other by 1.4 to 1.5 times; a weight change sees only that input, so where it acts is decided on the input side, by fitting every row of the answers' own computation. (2) trace-overlap-complete-registered: with every one of the 30,546 steps laid on the axis, the separation is still one connected region, places 142 to 313, 5.8 times the sampling variation, split-half 0.825. (3) state-overlap: the state right after each matrix's merge differs between the two patterns by several times chance over places 142 to 313 at every one of the 70 matrices, and that state is what the matrix controls and what the next matrix reads; the shared gaps of the turns do not add up to it. (4) Development readings with the revised solver on input-overlap's rows (the original model's rows, one matrix alone asked for the whole gap of its state, nothing written, no native run): attention of layer 0, the best candidate at 2^-17.8 of the system's strongest direction, 6.4% of the matrix, 0.66 of the squared ask left on the other half, the diverged steps reach 0.52 of theirs, and the change lies in the outputs with the largest learned scale; attention of layer 16, 2^-15.1, 18.8% of the matrix, 0.46 left on the other half, the diverged steps reach 0.73, the wrong answers' other steps move 0.013 and the correct answers' rows, which this rung does not fit, 0.037, against an ask of 0.073. In the build a matrix is asked only for what the ones before it left, so these are upper readings of what one matrix is asked, not predictions of the build. This is the A rung built under the one construction every rung will use, so that A2, B2, C2 and D2 differ only in whose rows are fitted and how they are weighed.
repeating_pattern_check: What has repeated, and what this run does about each. (a) The edit acted where nothing was asked, four times, because it was fitted only where it was asked; here every position of the wrong answers' own computation is a row of the fit, asked to move where the patterns diverge and to keep its turn elsewhere, the question's positions included. (b) The conversion from the trace to the weights was wrong or partial; here the fit is on the model's own expression for the state after the merge, with the learned scale and both projections inside, its exact derivative gives each step, every step is confirmed by that same expression at the changed weights, and the ridge is chosen on the edit as it is applied, rounded to the model's storage. (c) All matrices were sized on the original inputs; here they are solved in path order, each on what arrives with every earlier edit in the model. (d) A test of my own mechanics stood in for the hypothesis's test (the replay); here the passes that read the rows are construction only and are never reported as an outcome. (e) Several things changed at once, so runs did not compare; this run changes many things against a2-diverge on purpose and is not a one-variable comparison with it: it restarts the A rung under the construction the ladder will keep, and from here on a rung changes one thing. (f) A number chosen by eye; every quantity below is derived from a record. (g) Building machinery in place of the experiment; the solver is one file, and this run's outcome is the edited model's own answers. (h) What was asked was never added up along the path before an edit was built; state-overlap now records, at every matrix and place, what the asks imply, and the ask is the state the next matrix reads.

rule.members: The 30 wrong answers of the overlap (first incorrect calculation: the descent subtracted). Their rows are every generated step and every question position of their own computation, 21,583 rows per matrix. The 30 correct answers pass through the model in every pass and are read, but are not fitted: this rung has no protection.
rule.ask: At each of the 70 attention-output and feed-forward-down matrices, each row is asked for the direction the state had right after that matrix's merge in the original model, plus, at the generated steps of a wrong answer, the shared part of the gap between the correct and the wrong pattern of that state at the places that step is laid on, where the two patterns diverge at that matrix. A step laid on several places takes the average over them. What is asked of a matrix is that direction minus the one the row has now, with every earlier edit in the model: what the matrices before it left, and how the gated per-layer inputs answered them, is part of what it is asked.
rule.conversion: The direction of the state after the merge is unit(h + g*y/rms(y)), with y the matrix output for that row's input, g the learned scale after it and h the state it is added to. A change dW changes it by A(x dW) to first order, A = P_m diag(g) P_y / (|m| rms(y)): the norm takes out a change of size, the scale weighs each output, and a change along the merged state turns nothing. For a given ridge the change is the one that leaves the least of mean |wanted - state direction at the changed weights|^2 + ridge |dW|^2 over the fitted rows, the direction read by the model's own expression. It is found by preconditioned conjugate gradients on that expression: at every step the exact gradient at the current weights, a step along the conjugate direction sized by A there, kept only once the expression at the new weights confirms it and halved until it does; the preconditioner, a closed-form approximation of the system, is rebuilt whenever the conjugate direction fails. It ends when no step lowers what float32 can state, which is a truncated solve and is recorded as one, with its steps, the steps shortened, how it ended and how much of the gradient is left. The matrix is rounded to the model's BF16 storage and written only if, as rounded, it leaves less over the fitted rows than the matrix it replaces.
rule.path: The matrices are solved in path order, attention then feed-forward of each layer. Before each one the 60 answers' own text is given to the model as it stands, as text, and that matrix's input and incoming state are read at every position. The original states after each merge are read the same way on the original model first (baseline), so a row asked to keep its state is never asked to undo a difference between two ways of running the model; how far that reading is from the token-by-token recording of input-overlap is reported for every matrix, and beside the size of the move on the rows where a move is asked.
rule.test: The edited model answers the 60 questions and round one's 28 on its own, on GPU0, greedy; fields are judged original beside edited, failures only, damage to correct answers separately. Its answers to the 60 are recorded with the turns of their computation, laid along the same axis by the computation alone with the complete correspondence, and set against the original correct and wrong patterns: whether the answers that were wrong now follow the correct pattern from place 142 to 313, whether they still follow their own pattern elsewhere, and how far the answers that were correct moved. The passes used to build the edit are not a test. The summary of the traces leaves out the first merge, whose turn is mostly the token's own embedding and so follows the tokens written; it is read apart.

shared_part.derivation: max(0, 1 - chance / gap) at each place and matrix, for the direction of the state after that matrix's merge: the squared gap between two group means is, on average, the squared shared gap plus what chance adds; chance is the sum over the two groups of the members' spread divided by their count.
shared_part.scales_with: the number of members in each group and their spread at that place and matrix

diverged.derivation: gap > 2 * chance at a place and matrix: two halves of one group of n differ, on average, by the spread over n/2 twice, which is twice chance. A place and matrix where the two groups are no further apart than that is one where they follow each other, and the row is asked to keep its state there.
diverged.scales_with: the number of members in each group and their spread at that place and matrix

ridge.derivation: Per matrix, on the rows its own pass reads (the same answers and positions as this record lists): the wrong answers are split in two halves, alternating as in the overlap. A candidate ridge is judged by the edit as it would be applied: each half is fitted by the conversion above, rounded to BF16, and what it leaves on the other half is read with the model's own expression. The search starts at the system's strongest direction, where the edit is small, and walks by factors of two towards a weaker ridge while that leaves less (towards a stronger one if the first weaker step does not), each fit started from the one before; it then narrows between the neighbours of the best by golden section until its two inner candidates differ by less than rounding to BF16 moves that same number. That last rule only ends the search: it is not a claim that the candidates are the same, and the factor of two only spaces the candidates tried. The ridge is the best candidate evaluated. Leaving the matrix as it is is one of the candidates and wins when none leaves less than it. The curve need not have one minimum and the walk follows one branch: the value is the best found, and every candidate, with the size of its change, how alike the two halves' changes are and how its fits ended, is kept in build.jsonl. It selects the balance of the fit on the wrong answers only; it does not see rows off their own text, and it is not evidence that the edit carries to other questions.
ridge.scales_with: the matrix, its inputs after the earlier edits, the number of answers and how much of the ask recurs across them

prediction.expected_observation: Building: the middle layers reach most of what they are asked; later matrices are asked for less than the original gap of their state, because the earlier edits already carried part of it; the rows asked to keep their state drift by a small part of the move. Answering on its own, the edited model stays on the path where the two groups follow each other: it reads the question and writes the calculation, unlike a2-sent and a2-diverge, which left at the ninth token. The traces of the answers that were wrong lie nearer the correct pattern than before from place 142 to 313 and stay with their own pattern elsewhere. If the hypothesis holds, more of the 30 wrong answers have the available energy right than not. Having no protection, this rung also moves the correct answers where the patterns diverge, and some of the 30 correct answers are expected to break; which ones is what B2 will protect.
prediction.failures_only: Per wrong answer, its fields before and after, and where its own trace lies against the two patterns. Correct answers that break are listed separately. Round one's 28 are scored beside them.

would_weaken_it: The hypothesis: the edited model stays on the path, the traces of the answers that were wrong follow the correct pattern across places 142 to 313, and those answers still subtract the descent. The construction, not the hypothesis: the model leaves the path where the groups follow each other, or the traces do not move towards the correct pattern although the passes said the rows did; either means the edit built from given text does not hold when the model writes its own, and the run does not test the hypothesis.

revisions.made: After the baseline of the original model was read and before any pass of the build. No edit existed and no outcome of this run was known.
revisions.what: The target moved from the turn of each merge to the direction of the state right after each matrix's merge (target_source is now state-overlap; ask, conversion, path, shared_part and diverged follow). The ridge is chosen on the edit as applied, not on a closed-form approximation; leaving a matrix unchanged competes; a matrix is written only if its rounded form leaves less. The solver is one conjugate-gradient loop on the model's own expression and reports how it ended. stored_precision is gone: BF16 keeps seven bits after the leading one, not eight, and a storage step never belonged in a solver's stopping test; rounding is now applied to each candidate and measured.
revisions.why: Astra's review of the first solver (the ridge was selected on one estimator and another was applied; no status; unconditional write) and, while fixing it, the reading that the first attention matrix was being asked mostly for the gap of the token embeddings, which led to adding up what all the asks imply along the path. The first declaration's development readings (3.8% and 6.2% of the matrix changed, 0.43 and 0.35 left on the other half, at layer 16) were made with the first solver on turn targets and no longer describe this run.

revisions.made: While the build was running: 16 of the 70 matrices were written. The edited model did not exist yet and had answered nothing.
revisions.what: The test reads the edited model's own answers a second way, beside the declared reading of the turns: the state after each matrix's merge, against the correct and the wrong pattern of state-overlap, with the same correspondence (laid by the computation alone) and the same weights (the shared gap, where the patterns diverge). The turns of a step add up exactly to those states from the direction the step starts with, which is now kept with each trace (start.npy). The reading also reports how far the answers that were wrong are from the original correct pattern, not only from the correct answers as edited, and the size of the state after each merge, edited over original. Nothing of the members, the ask, the conversion, the path, the parameters or the prediction changes. overlay-states.npz is added to the outputs.
revisions.why: The revision above moved the ask from the turn of each merge to the state after each matrix and left the test reading only the turns. state-overlap showed that turn gaps do not add up to state gaps, so the turns alone cannot say whether the edit did, on the model's own answers, what it was aimed at; the prediction (the traces of the answers that were wrong lie nearer the correct pattern from place 142 to 313) is read both ways and both are reported. The size is Astra's point in review: the target holds the direction of the state only, so its size can change without any penalty and change the ratios the later merges see. The new reading was run on the original answers as if they were the edited model's: every answer read as unmoved, sizes 1.000, and the states rebuilt from the turns agreed with the baseline rows to 0.01 of the gap.

revisions.made: After the build was stopped at 18 of the 70 matrices (layers 0 to 8). No answer of the edited model existed.
revisions.what: The build stops here. The model as it stands, with 18 matrices edited and the 52 later ones untouched, is tested as declared: its own answers to the 60 questions and round one's 28, and its own traces against the patterns, in both readings.
revisions.why: The 19th matrix (layer 9 attention) left the regime the solver was built for: nearly every step shortened and minutes per candidate, where the same matrix on the original model's rows fits in seconds. Read row by row before that matrix, the state of the half-edited model on the given text was: on the wrong answers' steps where a move is asked, 0.55 of the move delivered along it and 0.128 rms beside it (the move is 0.125 rms), so 1.39 times further from the target in squared distance than before any edit; on their steps asked to stay, 0.107 rms from the original; on the correct answers' steps, 0.148 rms at the same places and 0.116 elsewhere. The declared construction prediction (the rows asked to keep their state drift by a small part of the move) is contradicted: they drift by about the whole move. Each matrix was asked for the whole gap at once; it reaches part of it and moves every row beside it, and the later matrices inherit both. Continuing would add hours of the same compounding. The model's own answers are the judge of what exists. Marcos asked on November 10 whether an optimizer step and its size were missing; this is where that question lands, and it is taken up in the next run, not here.
